read: A cardiology-heavy weekend. AHA 2026 delivered two high-profile outcome failures. Novartis's pelacarsen cut Lp(a) by ~78% with zero MACE benefit (HR 1.02), which puts the Lp(a) hypothesis itself in question and hits read-through for Amgen and Lilly. Novo's IL-6 bet ziltivekimab also landed flat in NEJM. Against that, Vir's pivotal HDV win and argenx's $1.15bn move for an oral macrocyclic peptide platform show capital still chasing de-risked late-stage assets and platform tuck-ins. Policy risk is now being litigated rather than just priced in: BIO has sued to block the GLOBE MFN pilot. Overall tone is constructive but selective. The IPO window is open (Rezera prices this week), China-sourced assets now make up over half of big pharma's $50m+ upfront licensing deals, and outcome-trial risk in novel CV mechanisms just got repriced.

items.headline: Novartis: pelacarsen Lp(a)HORIZON full data show no cardiovascular benefit despite ~78% Lp(a) lowering
items.detail: MACE 12.3% vs 12.1% placebo, HR 1.02 (0.90–1.15) in 8,350 secondary-prevention patients over 4.7 yrs median; no signal even at Lp(a) ≥90 mg/dL, and discontinuations from AEs were 20.6% vs 7.5%. This is the first Lp(a) outcomes trial and it sets up a binary for Amgen's olpasiran (OCEAN(a)) and Lilly's lepodisiran (ACCLAIM-Lp(a)); the bull case now rests on siRNAs' deeper knockdown and cleaner tolerability.

items.headline: Vir Biotechnology: Phase 3 ECLIPSE 1 hits in chronic hepatitis delta with tobevibart + elebsiran
items.detail: Primary composite (HDV RNA undetectable + ALT normalisation at wk 48) 44% vs 0% in the delayed-treatment arm (p<0.0001); undetectable HDV RNA 79% (85% in cirrhotics); one grade 3 treatment-related AE. ECLIPSE 2/3 data are due Q1 2027 and the US filing mid-2027. Stock rose 11% to $12.21 on Friday into the AASLD readout (about $2.1bn market cap).

items.headline: argenx to acquire Unnatural Products for up to $1.15bn
items.detail: $550m upfront plus CVRs tied to development and regulatory milestones, closing by year-end. Buys an AI-guided oral macrocyclic peptide discovery engine, which gives argenx an oral route against immunology targets beyond the FcRn franchise.

items.headline: BIO sues to block the Trump administration's GLOBE most-favoured-nation Medicare pricing model
items.detail: Filed Friday in the N.D. California with two California biotech trade groups, arguing that GLOBE (pegging Medicare drug prices to peer countries) exceeds CMS's statutory authority. This is the first direct legal test of the MFN demonstration route, and it lands days after Democrats took both chambers of Congress.

items.headline: Novo Nordisk: full ZEUS data at AHA/NEJM confirm ziltivekimab failed to cut MACE
items.detail: IL-6 and a second inflammation biomarker fell, but heart attacks, strokes and deaths did not (topline HR 0.99, July). HERMES and ATHENA were already halted. This is another dent in Novo's post-GLP-1 diversification story and in the IL-6/inflammation CV thesis.

items.headline: Moderna Q3 beat; full-year revenue growth guide raised to 15–25%
items.detail: Revenue $1.3bn (+29% y/y), with vaccine sales of $1.27bn against the ~$891m consensus cited by William Blair, on global COVID uptake. Guidance was raised from ~10% growth.

items.headline: Agios cuts more than 100 R&D roles (over 35% of R&D) as FDA pushes mitapivat SCD decision to 1 February 2027
items.detail: The PDUFA moved from 1 November after FDA asked for more on a potential safety protocol and is weighing a REMS. Agios is preserving cash ahead of its most important label expansion.

items.headline: Rezera sets terms for a ~$200m Nasdaq IPO (RZRA), pricing expected this week
items.detail: 16.7m shares at $11–13; Jefferies, TD and Cantor running the books. Lead asset is ruvonoflast, an oral NLRP3 inhibitor with two Phase 2s done in cardiometabolic disease and a Phase 3 in PAD planned for 1H27. It is a test of IPO appetite for inflammation-CV after this weekend's AHA misses.

items.headline: JPMorgan: China-sourced assets now account for 51% of big pharma licensing deals with $50m+ upfront
items.detail: Up from 18% in 2023, 26% in 2024 and 39% in 2025. Chinese licensors took 65% of upfront cash YTD, with ~$5.7bn of upfronts and equity through Q3, already above full-year 2025.

items.headline: Merck/Moderna: 99% of vaccine-arm patients in INTerpath-001 received a manufactured intismeran dose
items.detail: 82% of screened patients had enough tissue and 91% of those got the full neoantigen set. These manufacturing-feasibility numbers matter for the personalised cancer vaccine launch case (recurrence/death HR 0.58).

items.headline: Voyager and C4 Therapeutics disclose workforce cuts in Q3 filings
items.detail: Voyager took ~$1.4m in restructuring charges (headcount not disclosed); C4 called its cut a small early-2026 realignment.

items.headline: Agenus: bot/bal shows long-term survival in more than half of refractory MSS colorectal cancer patients at SITC
items.detail: Company-reported long-term survival data; the debate about regulatory path continues.

items.headline: Aulos Bioscience: imneskibart (IL-2) Phase 2 activity in checkpoint-refractory melanoma and NSCLC at SITC
items.detail: Company says results compare favourably with historical benchmarks; early, single-arm data.

items.headline: Sarepta's new CEO projects confidence on execution as DMD competitors close in
Lilly: Canada's CDA-AMC recommends reimbursement of Kisunla (donanemab) in early Alzheimer's
items.detail: An incremental ex-US access win for the anti-amyloid class.
